fields.reasoning: Run 01M73CQ4D71CW038ZBNSQB1SJF journalled signoff owner (source workflow docs) and still signed off under rule autonomous: internal/run/signoff.go checks only State.Autonomous. Guarding at the step covers every start path (daemon dispatch, queued run start, run start --autonomous, nested review workflows), which is what the milestone's owner-signs-each-page Decisions need. A signoff stage that is owner only by the rhiza.autonomy.signoff setting keeps today's behaviour, out of this bug's scope.
fields.statement: The signoff step itself honours the workflow's declared signoff stage: when the run recorded signoff = owner from its workflow, it waits for the owner even in an autonomous run, rather than relying on the daemon dropping --autonomous at start

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/run/... covers the signoff step with Autonomous set and the recorded signoff stage owner from a workflow (waits, no autonomous signoff entry), auto from a workflow and from the setting (signs off under rule autonomous), and a journal without the record; a new testscript cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/run-signoff-workflow-owner.txtar runs run start --autonomous on a workflow declaring [autonomy] signoff = owner with fake agents, sees the run stop at signoff with no rule-autonomous sign-off in rhiza run status --json, then rhiza run approve lets it finish; review-signoff-autonomous, workflow-stage-autonomy and run-autonomy-source scripts pass unchanged
fields.statement: A signoff step waits for the owner whenever its run's workflow declares the signoff stage owner, even when the run is autonomous: it journals no sign-off of rule autonomous, stops with the owner's sign-off wait naming the workflow's declaration, and passes only on rhiza run approve (or goes back on request-changes); a run whose workflow declares signoff auto or nothing still signs off under rule autonomous; the declaration is read from the run's recorded stage autonomy, from the top-level workflow, so a signoff step in a nested workflow obeys it too, and a journal that predates that record falls back to the started workflow definition's declaration
